reason: T-001, T-004, and T-005 have event assertions that are structurally impossible to pass given Move test framework semantics. In all three tests, event::events_by_type<VaultCreated or TriggerFired>() is called in a test_scenario transaction context AFTER the transaction in which the event was emitted — separated by at least one test_scenario::next_tx() call. The Move test VM resets the event buffer on each next_tx() call (confirmed by Sui framework's own test_scenario_tests.move line 1092: assert_eq!(event::num_events(), 0) after next_tx, and confirmed empirically on Sui 1.69.2). Specifically: T-001 emits VaultCreated in test.next_tx(OWNER) block 2 but reads events_by_type<VaultCreated> in block 3 (after a second next_tx call); T-004 emits TriggerFired in test.next_tx(KEEPER) block 3 but reads events_by_type<TriggerFired> AFTER test.next_tx(OWNER) and test.next_tx(KEEPER); T-005 has the same pattern as T-004. The implementation (tpsl_vault.move) is correct: it emits the events in the right places, and 4 of 7 tests pass (T-002 withdraw before fire, T-003 non-owner abort, T-006 trigger condition not met, T-007 withdraw after fire). Only the event-count assertions in T-001, T-004, T-005 fail because the tests query events across transaction boundaries. The fix requires either (a) moving the event assertions into the same next_tx block where the emitting function is called, or (b) using a different event-capture mechanism. Both require modifying the sealed test file, which is forbidden.
notes: Implementation staged at files/independent/03-tpsl-vault/move/sources/tpsl_vault.move. All struct fields, error codes, entry functions, read accessors, and event field shapes are correct. 4/7 tests pass. The 3 failing tests (T-001, T-004, T-005) all contain event::events_by_type<T> calls that span next_tx boundaries — a Move test framework constraint that cannot be worked around from the implementation side.
